Closing sets closedAt; archiving sets archivedAt and keeps an earlier closedAt; reopening clears both. The version goes up by one and last_edited_at does not change. A request for the status the investigation already has answers 200 with the same version and writes nothing, whatever expectedVersion it carries. A stale expectedVersion is CONFLICT without a reason. Closing, archiving and reopening are audited as investigation.close, investigation.archive and investigation.reopen, with a success event recorded after the change is committed (a failed write records a failed event instead); if the sink rejects the success event the change stays and the answer is INTERNAL_ERROR. An identifier that does not exist, is not a UUID, belongs to another user or is deleted gives the same 404.

Each document is at most 1048576 bytes of JSON. A reference of a keyed entity type must be a token of this deployment for this source and type. Filters on personal-data properties are not stored. notes is required (a string of at most 10,000 characters with no NUL and no unpaired surrogate, or null): a client writes back the note it last received. The note is part of the content, and every draft answer carries it. A write whose content equals the stored draft changes nothing and answers the same version. The investigation's last_edited_at moves only when the content changed. An identifier that does not exist, is not a UUID, belongs to another user or is deleted gives the same 404; an investigation whose source is not available as it was gives CONFLICT.

The source is the one the reference names. The answer holds the type, the two ends (their reference, title and entity type), the time the mapping's observed_at gives, the mapped properties the relationship holds other than its stable ID and observed time, which have their own fields, its quality flags and evidence. evidence is { status: available, records } with each record { sourceRecordId, linkable } or { property, unreadable: true }, or { status: not-available, code: EVIDENCE_NOT_AVAILABLE } when the source kept no record for the relationship; that is a state of an ordinary answer and never an error response. linkable is true only when the mapping gives the evidence a link; no URL is ever sent. mask asks for the personal-data fields to be masked, and the end titles with them. There is no confidence or score. For an aggregate reference { sourceId, aggregate: { type, from, to } } (all relationships of one type between two entities that have no usable stable ID; the keys in that order) the answer has semantics aggregate: the member count (exact over every member, or unknown with no number when the count could not be read in time, with a warning saying why), the earliest and latest observed time, and a sample of at most the smaller of 25 and the source max_page members, each as its observed time and mapped properties only, in order observed-newest (the row maps an observed time) or source-order (the first members the source returns, in its own order). more is the members not shown. There is no paging, and no element ID, member reference, record ID or URL is ever sent.

post.summary: Search a source for the entities whose search properties equal a text
post.description: Matches the whole text, as stored and case-sensitive, against every configured, indexed search property of the source in one read through the gate, and as the integer too when the text is a canonical 64-bit integer. The answer holds at most cap entities in exact (25, or the source's max_page when lower); counts.exact is exact when the group has no next page and a lowerBound of the hits held (cap, or fewer when normalization left rows out of a capped read) when the read found more, and exactNextCursor is then the cursor of the next page of the group (POST /v1/search/entities/more); each of related and evidence holds its own nextCursor the same way; searchable is false when no property was left to search. The text is 1 to 200 characters. entityTypes and matchModes (a non-empty list of different names each, absent when the search is not narrowed, refused with typeahead true) narrow the search to those entity types of the mapping of the source (the exact and the related group; the evidence group is not narrowed by entity type) and to the groups of those match modes (exact, related, evidence; a group that is not chosen is not read and is not searchable in the answer); a name the mapping does not know is INVALID_REQUEST. mask asks for the personal-data fields of the entities to be masked, and a personal-data property is then not searched. dropped and warnings are the normalize stage's: rows left out, by reason, and one sentence for each. disabledTypes names each search property that was not searched, with its entity type and why (index-unavailable: no online index; index-building: its index is populating; index-failed: its index failed), and typeSearched false when none of the properties of the type was searched; the other properties of the type are searched. related is the second group: the records whose reference properties (named by the mapping) hold the text, from one read of their own with its own limit, capped and counted like exact (counts in related.count, scope search:related); the related read adds nothing to exact or to its count: an entity is in exact only through its own exact match, and one that is both appears in both groups. related.searchable is false when no reference property was left to read (none configured, only personal-data ones while masked, or every type left out) and related.disabledTypes names each reference property left out the same way. evidence is the third group: the relationships whose evidence properties (named by the mapping) hold the text, from one read of their own with its own limit, capped and counted like exact (counts in evidence.count, scope search:evidence, in supporting relationships: a stored hit is one, an aggregate hit its members). A hit on a relationship row that has a stable_id is { supports, records, rules }: supports is the stored reference { sourceId, type, from, to, stableId } of the relationship. A hit on a row with no stable_id is { aggregate, members, memberCount, rules }: aggregate is { type, from, to } with the references of both ends, members are its relationships on this page, each { records, observedAt? } (a member has no ID: the element ID of the source never leaves the server, and the next page continues from a position the signed cursor holds), and memberCount is the members listed, a lowerBound when another page may hold more. records are the values of all the evidence properties of a relationship, each { sourceRecordId } or, for a value that is neither text nor a number, { property, unreadable: true }; rules are the configured rules of the mapping that use its relationship type. evidence.searchable is false when no relationship row was left to read, and evidence.disabledRelationshipTypes names each evidence property not searched with its row and the same reasons. With typeahead true the text is 2 to 200 characters and the answer also holds startsWith: the entities whose search property starts with the text, apart from the entities in exact, with its own count (exact up to and including cap, a lowerBound above it, never counted as exact matches), dropped and warnings; it is one more read, capped at cap and not paged (it has no nextCursor, so a common prefix never makes the source read every match), and shares the one schema read. A type-ahead request reads neither the related nor the evidence group: their searchable is false in its answer. A group whose read failed with a code of its own (QUERY_TIMEOUT with timeoutMs, SOURCE_BUSY, RATE_LIMITED or INTERNAL_ERROR) while another group answered is empty, has a count of quality unknown with no value, and is named in failures (always present, empty when every read answered); a retry repeats the whole search. When every group that was read fails, or an error means the same for every group, the search fails as a whole with the status and error of the read. facets (every answer that is not a type-ahead answer; a type-ahead answer holds neither facets nor filters) is the size of the whole match set, whatever is selected, from one read of its own: searchable is false when no target was left to count; otherwise entityType holds an entry for each entity type that has an eligible search or reference target (the entities of that type matched by either, each counted once), matchMode an entry for each match mode with an eligible target (exact, related, evidence; evidence in supporting relationships) and total the entities matched by any target; every count is exact up to and including the source's count cap (heavy_op_threshold, 500 by default) and a lowerBound of the cap above it, and an exact count is never lower than the hits its group holds (scopes search:facet:entityType, search:facet:matchMode, search:facet:total), and none is the sum of others. A facet counts the matches in the source, a group shows what the normalize stage can name, so a facet can be higher than its group by the records normalization dropped. The facet read is one more read and is not a result group: when it fails with a code of its own it is named in failures with the group facets, facets is then searchable with an unknown total and no entry, and every group is kept; it is never counted among the groups that failed. filters is the selection the answer was made for (entity types and match modes, each empty when the request did not narrow). The text is never logged and never part of an error.

post.summary: The next page of one group of a search
post.description: Reads the page after cursor of one group (exact, related or evidence) of the search the cursor came from, and only that group, through the gate, with the same masking, the same searched properties and the same index plan as the first page (the schema is read again for this request). text, mask and entityTypes are those of that search; entityTypes narrow exact and related as there. The startsWith group of a type-ahead answer has no next page: a request for it is INVALID_REQUEST. Pages follow the element ID order of the source, so no hit is on two pages and none is skipped. The answer is the group's next hits in that group's shape (nodes for exact, hits for related and evidence), count (the hits of this page: a lowerBound when nextCursor is present, exact when this is the last page; the group's count is the hits held before plus these), nextCursor, dropped and warnings. A cursor of another group, text, selection, source or person, an expired cursor or one with a changed byte is CURSOR_INVALIDATED. A read that fails with a code of its group (QUERY_TIMEOUT with timeoutMs, SOURCE_BUSY, RATE_LIMITED or INTERNAL_ERROR) is answered with 200 and failure, no hit and an unknown count, and the cursor that was sent can be sent again; any other failure fails the request with its own status and error. The text is never logged and never part of an error.

post.summary: The degree of a node by relationship type and direction, before anything is loaded
post.description: Counts the mapped relationships of one node, one count for each (relationship type, direction) pair of its entity type, in one read through the gate. A count read from the degree of the node (an entity type whose checks showed the server to answer that way) is exact whatever its size; a count read by the bounded read is exact up to and including the source's heavy_op_threshold and a lowerBound of that value above it, with one counts-capped warning for each pair read that way; byNeighborType gives the count by the entity type at the other end only where the pair has one mapped neighbor type, and unknown where it has several. total is the sum with the weakest quality of its parts, counted over the mapped relationship ends at the node, and is unknown when a sum would pass the largest safe integer. A pair whose count stopped at the cap (a lowerBound) takes the number of a degree property the mapping declares for that entity type and pair, as an estimated count, when the property holds a whole number above the cap; the count then carries observedAt when the mapping names a date property for it and the date can be read (the time the customer computed the number, never the time of the read). An exact count is never replaced, the cheap read never reads the property, and a value that cannot be taken leaves the lowerBound. A sum with a lowerBound part stays a lowerBound that adds the cap, not the estimate, for an estimated part; a count made from a single pair is the count of that pair with its observedAt, and a sum of two or more parts carries no observedAt. warnings name a capped count (counts-capped), a degree property whose value was not used (degree-property-ignored, once for a relationship type, with a fixed reason that names neither the value nor the property) and a second node with the same stable ID (duplicate-stable-id). A node that is not in the source, is of another entity type, or is in a source that is not configured or that the person may not read is NOT_FOUND, one answer for all. mask is part of the request because the answer is cached per mask setting; no property value is in it. heavyOpThreshold is the source's heavy_op_threshold, which the client judges an expansion by; it is a setting and not a count. No stable ID or count is logged.

post.summary: The rule-derived neighbors of an entity, counted and returned in one bounded read
post.description: Runs each derived rule of the mapping whose from type is the entity type of the node, in mapping order, in one read through the gate (one read for each rule, under one read slot): the other ends the rule finds, at most 25 (fewer when the source lowered max_page below 25), each with the first chain of nodes and relationships that supports it. The answer holds one result for each rule: the rule ID and version from the mapping, the count, and the other ends, the middle entities, the derived relationships and the supporting relationships of the derived relationships that were counted. The count is exact when the run read every other end the rule gives, and a lowerBound (the number that remained) when it stopped at the cap (25, or the lower max_page of the source); a derived relationship whose end or whose supporting relationship the person may not see is neither counted nor returned, and a count that stopped at the cap is never exact after such a relationship was dropped. A relationship type of the chain with no stable ID supports as an aggregate relationship whose member count is a lowerBound. An entity type with no rule gives an empty list of results and reads nothing. When no rule finds anything, the answer is confirmed by one entity read through the gate (with its own audit event, and under its own read slot after the first is released), so that an exact zero for an entity that exists is told apart from a node that is not there. A node that is not in the source, is of another entity type, or is in a source that is not configured or that the person may not read is NOT_FOUND, one answer for all. mask is part of the request because the nodes follow it; while it is true a rule whose stop-list property is personal data is INVALID_REQUEST. No stable ID or count is logged.

The count is of relationships, not entities, and is never better than the weakest quality of its parts; when some named entity has no cached preview the answer is a lower bound from the others, and unknown, with no value, when they give none.

post.summary: Read again the entities and relationships a stored draft names, by reference
post.description: Reads through the gate, as the calling principal, the items of one source that a stored draft names: entities, stored relationships, aggregate relationships and derived relationships, each list at most 100 references. A draft holds references and never property values, so a reopened investigation gets its items back here. The call counts as one request; every item is read by the template the matching single read uses, so the masking, the count labels and the limits are those of the single reads. An item that no longer resolves is listed under missing, once, whatever the cause (gone from the source, a type or rule no longer mapped, or not readable by the person); nothing says which. The relationships come without their ends: the entities are asked for in the same or an earlier call. A derived relationship is returned only when its rule still finds it and every one of its ends and supports is readable. A reference of another source is SOURCE_MISMATCH; a reference of a keyed entity type that is not a token of this deployment for this source and type is INVALID_REQUEST. If a read fails, nothing is returned.

post.summary: One page of the neighbors of a node for each asked neighbor type
post.description: Reads one page of at most `limit` relationships (the source default page when absent; above the source maximum the answer is QUERY_BUDGET_EXCEEDED) for each asked neighbor type, newest first by the observed time of the mapping row and undated last, with the neighbor nodes. The types are read one after another under one read lease and the answer holds a page and a cursor for each; a failure in any of them answers the failure and no page. A cursor continues one type and is refused with CURSOR_INVALIDATED when altered, expired or minted for another source, person, policy version, sort, neighbor type, relationship types, direction or node. Relationships of a type with no stable ID are returned as aggregate relationships with their member count.

get.summary: The configured sources, with their state and a summary of their mapping
get.description: Returns every configured source in one response, ordered by id, with nextCursor always null: the configuration file defines the list and it is small, so it is not paged (an exception to the pagination convention). mappingSummary holds exact counts of configured definitions, not of graph data. lastTest summarizes the newest stored test made for the current connection and mapping of the source (null when there is none): when it ran, its outcome, the server product and version, the read-only check, and the degree status and warnings; it holds no address, credential or query text. It is read from the stored record of the product, not from the source. timeoutMs, when present, is the server-side transaction timeout in milliseconds, which the app shows a running request against. The list takes no query parameters.
